record.paper_title: Cooperative Games with Incomplete Information: Some Open Problems
record.context_brief: Generalized Nash program under incomplete information
record.original_question: In exchange economies with asymmetric information at the interim stage, which negotiation procedures can support a generalized Nash program that explains coalition formation and stable payoff distribution when coalitions communicate and block allocations under incomplete information?

evidence.quote: In general, the exploration of different negotiation procedures should be an important vehicle to tackle questions of coalition formation and stable payoff distribution. These questions, comprising a generalized Nash program, remain almost entirely unexplored in these settings.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a pure exchange economy with a finite set N of agents, a finite set Ω of states of nature, and a common prior μ on Ω. Each agent i ∈ N has a consumption set X_i ⊆ R^ℓ_+, a state-dependent utility u_i : X_i × Ω → R, an initial endowment e_i : Ω → X_i, and a private information partition F_i of Ω; the interim stage is the moment after each agent has observed her own element of F_i but before the state is publicly revealed. An allocation is a profile (x_i)_{i∈N} of state-contingent consumption bundles with Σ_i x_i(ω) = Σ_i e_i(ω) for every ω ∈ Ω, possibly subject to measurability constraints with respect to information sigma-algebras. A coalition S ⊆ N can communicate internally (pooling some or all of its members' private information according to a specified protocol) and may attempt to block a candidate allocation by proposing an S-feasible reallocation that interim-dominates it for every member of S given the communicated information.

Formulate a non-cooperative bargaining/negotiation procedure Γ — that is, an extensive-form game in which players (i) form coalitions, (ii) share private information according to explicit communication rules, and (iii) propose and accept or reject reallocations — whose set of (perfect Bayesian, sequential, or other appropriately specified) equilibrium outcomes coincides with a given cooperative interim solution concept C for economies with asymmetric information (for example, the interim core, the private core, the coarse or fine core, an interim bargaining set, or an interim value).

Problem. Identify and characterize negotiation procedures Γ that implement, in the above non-cooperative sense, cooperative interim solution concepts C for exchange economies with asymmetric information, and thereby realize a "generalized Nash program" explaining coalition formation and stable payoff distribution under incomplete information. In particular, determine for which solution concepts C such a procedure Γ exists, and provide a general construction relating the communication and blocking rules of Γ to the informational structure underlying C.
artifact.status_search_result: The generalized Nash program for cooperative games with incomplete information is explicitly described as almost entirely unexplored in the surveyed literature. Subsequent work (e.g., Serrano and collaborators on the Nash program; de Clippel–Serrano; Forges–Serrano surveys on cooperative games with incomplete information) continues to treat noncooperative implementation of interim cooperative solutions as a largely open research direction, with only isolated results for specific solution concepts. No comprehensive characterization is known.
